title: Orazaka pack manifest
description: The unit of distribution (ADR-037 §3.2). One directory, one manifest, one transactional install. Everything a pack contributes to the platform is declared here or in a file this manifest names; nothing about a pack is knowable only from a seed file.

apiVersion.description: Manifest grammar version. Bumped only for a breaking change to this schema, so an installer can refuse a bundle it cannot read rather than mis-reading it.

key.description: The bundle's stable identity. When `catalog` is present this is also the pack_key, mirrored opaquely into billing_pack with no FK (SEAM-001).

tier.description: What the pack needs from the platform. DATA reuses existing capabilities and ships no code; CAPABILITY adds in-process executors; WORKER brings its own out-of-process worker. Phase D installs DATA packs; the other two are declared so a manifest written today survives phases H and beyond.

distribution.description: Where the pack may be obtained. Read by the open-core split (phase G); recorded now so no pack has to be re-licensed later.

regulatoryClass.description: Drives the seven controls of phase I. STANDARD until that phase gives the other two teeth.

kind.description: How the pack reaches the user (ADR-061). VERTICAL: chosen and installed; the installation is a row that pins a version and records consent. TOOLKIT: an entitled actor simply has it; the installation is derived from entitlement and never stored, and a run resolves the latest published version once, at start. Orthogonal to `tier` and `regulatoryClass` — a TOOLKIT implies neither CAPABILITY nor STANDARD — and never read from the key: echo-toolkit is a VERTICAL.

requires.description: What must already be true of the platform for this pack to run.

orazakaVersion.description: A semver range. Recorded and reported; not yet enforced, because the platform does not version itself yet.

capabilities.description: Capabilities the pack CONTRIBUTES. A DATA pack declares none and reuses orazaka.core.*; the installer verifies every featureKey a blueprint names is routable either way, so an empty list is a claim the installer checks rather than a gap it ignores.

workers.description: Workers the pack brings (tier WORKER). Declared for phase H; the installer records nothing from this in phase D and says so rather than half-applying it.

catalog.description: The shelf entry: a `pack` row, its category and its bundling of Studios. OPTIONAL, and its absence is a real case rather than an oversight — trade-showcase and outbound-prospection are Studios that belong to no pack, and a manifest format that could not express today's catalogue would fail its first test. Without it the bundle ships Studios only, and no pack/pack_i18n/pack_studio/billing_pack row is written.

category.description: The category to create if it does not exist. Omit to require that the shelf already exists — an install then fails loudly rather than inventing a shelf under a typo.

pricing.description: What the pack costs and what buying it grants — the billing_pack half. Required when `catalog` is present, because a pack row with no price is unsellable and a PAID Studio with no pack is unreachable.

studios.description: The Studios this bundle ships. At least one: a bundle that ships nothing runnable is a packaging error, not a pack.

scopeGuard.description: The domain this pack REFUSES to answer in. Required for regulatoryClass SENSITIVE and rejected at install without it, because a control that is optional is not a control (ADR-051). The engine holds the interceptor and never the subject: a legal pack refusing legal advice and a medical pack refusing diagnosis are the same code and two manifests.

refusedTerms.description: Terms whose presence in the turn refuses it. Matched case-insensitively on word boundaries, never as substrings.

refusal.description: The exact answer given instead. Written by the pack's author, never generated — a fixed response is the only kind that can be reviewed before it is given.

consent.description: The versioned consent a REGULATED pack requires before it may be installed. Consent is to a STATEMENT, not to a checkbox: bumping the version stops every existing installation until its owner agrees again, and that cost is the point (GDPR Art. 9, Loi 25 — health data is a special category).

version.description: MAJOR.MINOR. Changing it re-asks every installation.

statement.description: What the user is agreeing to, in plain language.

safety.description: A REGULATED pack's crisis handling. The response is FIXED and reviewed by a person — a model asked to compose a crisis reply produces a number that looks like a crisis line, and someone will dial it. A region with no verified resource is a region the pack does not install in.

crisisTerms.description: What this pack treats as crisis content, in its own language.

safetyReviewRef.description: What the human review was, so the claim has something behind it.

resources.description: region → the verified crisis line that answers there.

sourceUrl.description: Where the contact was read. An unsourced crisis number is the one thing this pack must never ship.

verifiedOn.description: When it was last read there. These change.

allOf.description: A catalogued pack must carry a price: `billing_pack_entitlement` is what makes the purchase usable, and PackCoherenceRules fails the build when a pack_studio row has no matching grant (ADR-036 invariant #3).
A PAID Studio needs a pack to open a checkout for — the same invariant the studio table spells as studio_pricing_needs_package.
A TOOLKIT is never REGULATED: consent is recorded on an installation, and a TOOLKIT's installation is derived. The database refuses the row too (ck_pack_toolkit_not_regulated).

A TOOLKIT declares neither consent nor safety, and has a catalog entry: consent and the region-chosen crisis reply are answered from an installation row it does not have, and its kind is stored on the pack row a catalog entry writes (ck_pack_toolkit_no_installation_controls).

key.description: kebab-case and stable. It is a primary key in three databases and an opaque join between two of them; renaming one is a migration, not an edit.

iconKey.description: Resolves in the design-system Icon registry. Unresolvable keys render nothing, so this is checked by eye, not by the installer.

featureKey.description: A capability key as orazaka_capabilities holds it.

routingKey.description: WHICH process drains it. The first of the two dispatch discriminants (ADR-038).

handlerKey.description: WHICH code path runs it — the JobExecutor whose handlerKey() equals this. The second discriminant.

billableUnit.description: Omit where the unit is a property of the MODEL rather than of the capability — credit_pricebook keeps `unit` out of its key for exactly that reason.

inputSchema.description: What a CALLER MAY PASS, as a JSON Schema: types, `required`, defaults, and `format: prose | asset-id` where a composer must know which of its two holdings fills the input (ADR-068 §3). This is what payloadTemplate carried as an untyped string of ${placeholders} (ADR-069).

outputSchema.description: What a SUCCESSFUL EXECUTION PUBLISHES, with types. Every {{steps.<out>.<field>}} link in every blueprint references one of these fields, and until ADR-069 nothing declared them — so no rule could check a link and the one hand-written table that tried was wrong.

capability.description: What a pack CONTRIBUTES to the registry: dispatch (routingKey, handlerKey), contract (inputSchema, outputSchema), billing, and whether it is on. It carried a label, an icon, a uriPath, an httpMethod and a payloadTemplate until ADR-069 §5 — the registry's UI-manifest half, whose endpoints door 1 owned and whose display names now live in the pack's i18n.

entitlementKey.description: studio.<studioKey>. Read verbatim by EntitlementSnapshot.allows, which is why adding a Studio needs zero billing code.

blueprint.description: The path, relative to the bundle root, of the blueprint JSON for this Studio's version.
